anna: Quick heads-up — I pushed mnemo-embed-v2 quant6 to staging for a smoke onboarding. Short-query recall@5 dropped ~8% vs fp16 and clusters look split in UMAP. Sharing artifacts.
ravi: Thanks — what dataset / eval slice? short queries only or full distribution?
lena: pinging eval-bot for the numeric dump + silhouette/recall per-length bucket.
eval-bot: result summary for run mnemo-embed-v2|quant6|staging:
```
dataset: redwood-ssim-10k
metric: recall@5 overall: 0.762 (fp16 baseline: 0.832)
short-queries (<32 tokens) recall@5: 0.601 (baseline 0.695)
long-queries (>=128 tokens) recall@5: 0.810 (baseline 0.823)
silhouette mean: 0.23 (baseline 0.41)
cluster-count(kmeans, k=200): 244 (baseline 198)
```
anna: ugh — big delta on short queries. I also noticed centroid drift on several high-density clusters (labels: faq, howto, api-error). Attached UMAP snapshot link: https://redwood-internal/umap/mnemo-quant6/169.png
ravi: possible causes: per-channel quantization mismatch for small magnitudes, or KV cache padding interaction. Did you run per-channel vs per-tensor quant experiments?
anna: only per-tensor so far. I can run per-channel next. Also will try symmetric vs asymmetric clipping.
lena: also try eval with L2-normalization toggled — we normalize embeddings on write but staging retrieval uses dot-product. That mismatch can amplify quant noise for short vectors.
anna: good catch. On staging we normalize after quantization (because the client code uses L2 post-process). I will try normalizing before quant and compare.
eval-bot: queued experiments: [per-channel-quant, pre-quant-norm, asymmetric-clip]. ETA ~ 40m.
ops-bot: FYI reserving an extra staging GPU for the per-channel runs at 17:40 UTC.
ravi: if per-channel fixes >4% on short queries, we should consider shipping a quant profile for mnemo-embed-v2 dedicated builds. If not, fallback plan is fp16 short-query shard + quant for long queries (routing by token length).
lena: also propose a quick classification test: take 500 short-query pairs with known positives and compute pairwise cosine shift distributions (fp16 vs quant6). If distribution mean shifts >0.02, mark as suspect.
anna: on it — I'll post the pairwise diff hist and brief triage notes when the jobs finish. Thanks all :thumbsup:
__note: Document generated for dataset; contains single Slack thread as continuous string.
